title: React ui-v2 internationalization — add Nederlands, Deutsch, and Francais
goal: Make the React ui-v2 operator interface available in Dutch, German, and French, while keeping the existing English copy as the default/fallback. Operators must be able to switch language from the UI, have the preference persist, and see core screens rendered without mixed-language navigation or untranslated placeholders.
scope: (1) Add a deterministic i18n layer to ui-v2 using either an existing project dependency or a minimal local translation helper if no dependency exists. (2) Add locale files for en, nl, de, and fr. (3) Translate the primary operator shell, navigation, Settings, Mission Control / active run surfaces, findings/status labels, common buttons, loading/error/empty states, and safety/approval copy. (4) Add a visible language selector in ui-v2 that persists the selected locale in localStorage and falls back to English when a key is missing. (5) Add tests and browser proof for Dutch, German, and French at desktop and mobile widths.
generation_reason: Operator asked: 'Kun jij een taak aanmaken voor je ui en deze achteraan zetten en zorgen dat de ui-v2 ook in het nederlands, duits en frans is.' This task is queued at the end and does not change the active NEXT_TASK.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement until this package is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md AND ANTI_DRIFT.md + SESSION_PROMPT.md have been loaded.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: UI internationalization only. Do not change backend behavior, assessment logic, runner behavior, prompts, findings schema, or security decisions.
constraints.no_runtime_translation_service: All translations must be static repo-backed locale resources. No external translation API call at runtime.
constraints.fallback_language: English remains the default and fallback language when a translation key is missing.
constraints.operator_safety_copy: Approval, scope, kill-switch, credential, destructive-action, and evidence warnings must be translated carefully and remain semantically equivalent across all locales.

success_criteria: Metric: ui-v2 supports four locales: en, nl, de, fr.
Metric: language selection persists across reloads via localStorage and defaults to English on first visit.

Metric: core shell/navigation, Settings, Mission Control, findings/status labels, common controls, loading/error/empty states, and approval/safety copy render in Dutch, German, and French without obvious English fallback on the tested paths.
Metric: i18n coverage test fails when required locale files are missing keys present in English.
Browser: Playwright screenshots or assertions prove Dutch, German, and French on desktop and mobile widths.
Lint/typecheck: ui-v2 lint/typecheck pass or any pre-existing unrelated failures are explicitly separated from this task's changes.
must_not_touch: Capability pack registry / validation / approval / runtime binding flows

required_checks: cd ui-v2 && npm run test -- --run i18n
acceptance_criteria: Live/browser: language selector switches to Nederlands, Deutsch, and Francais without full-page errors.
Live/browser: selected language survives reload and route changes.
Live/browser: screenshots or Playwright assertions cover at least Mission Control and Settings in nl/de/fr at desktop and mobile widths.
Coverage: locale key parity test proves nl/de/fr contain all required keys present in en.
Documentation/result file records intentionally untranslated product names, acronyms, API identifiers, and security terms.

before_promotion: NEXT_TASK.md must contain this task as the single active task.
ANTI_DRIFT.md and SESSION_PROMPT.md must be loaded.
Existing ui-v2 build/lint baseline must be captured so unrelated pre-existing failures are not hidden by this task.
after_completion: Update DONE_LOG.md with build/lint/test results, browser proof links, and the i18n coverage summary.
Promote the next queued package into NEXT_TASK.md or leave operator-directed promotion note if this was the last queued task.

out_of_scope: Changing assessment, runner, approval, scope, or evidence behavior
